plan: Given the private value of $28, I should aim to bid just below this value to maximize profit while still potentially winning the auction. A rational strategy would involve bidding slightly less than the value, as bidding the full value or more would result in zero or negative profit if I win. Since values are drawn independently each round and all bidders are rational, a bid slightly below $28, such as $27.9, is optimal to potentially win while ensuring a positive profit margin.

My value exceeds the maximum possible value of $20, an anomaly. Rational bidders bid below their value to ensure profit. I should bid slightly above $20 to win, but not too high to minimize payments. A bid of $20.1 should secure the win, as it is slightly above the maximum value others might have, ensuring a profit of $4.9 if the highest other bid is $20.

The optimal strategy in a private value auction is to bid slightly above the expected second-highest value, which rational bidders would also aim for. Given my value is $20, I should bid slightly lower to ensure profit while still being competitive. Since values range from $0 to $20, a rational bid could be around $13-$15, balancing winning chances and profit margin. I'll bid $15, expecting others to bid slightly below their values, ensuring I win if their values are lower and still gain profit if they are close.
